items.title: Section: The Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation Opens

items.zh: 如是已說趣入地。云何出離地？嗢拕南曰：若世間離欲，如是出世間。及此二資糧，是名出離地。謂若由世間道而趣離欲，若由出世道而趣離欲，若此二道所有資糧，總略為一，名出離地。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the first yogic process, the third chapter, the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation, part one. …Thus the Ground of Entry has already been explained. What is the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation? …The summary verse says: mundane detachment, and likewise supramundane detachment, together with the provisions for both — this is called the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation. …Whether one sets out towards detachment by the mundane path, or sets out towards detachment by the supramundane path, or whether it is the provisions belonging to both paths — all of this together, in brief, is called the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation.

items.title: Mundane Detachment: Coarse Below, Peaceful Above, Level by Level

items.zh: 云何名為由世間道而趣離欲？謂如有一，於下欲界觀為麁相，於初靜慮離生喜樂若定、若生觀為靜相。彼由多住如是觀時，便於欲界而得離欲，亦能證入最初靜慮。如是復於初靜慮上，漸次如應，一切下地觀為麁相，一切上地觀為靜相。彼由多住如是觀時，便於乃至無所有處而得離欲，亦能證入乃至非想非非想處。如是名為由世間道而趣離欲。除此更無若過若增。
items.en: What is called setting out towards detachment by the mundane path? It is like one who observes the lower desire realm as coarse, and observes the joy and ease born of seclusion in the first absorption — whether attained through concentration or through rebirth there — as peaceful. Through repeatedly dwelling in this contemplation, one thereby attains detachment from the desire realm, and is able to enter the first absorption. In just this way, ascending progressively from the first absorption onward, one observes every lower level as coarse, and every higher level as peaceful. Through repeatedly dwelling in this contemplation, one thereby attains detachment all the way up to the sphere of nothingness, and is able to enter even the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. This is called setting out towards detachment by the mundane path. Beyond this, there is nothing further to exceed it, and nothing further to add.

items.zh: 云何名為由出世道而趣離欲？
items.en: What is called setting out towards detachment by the supramundane path?

items.title: Supramundane Detachment: Seeds Stored Away Versus Seeds Burnt by Fire

items.zh: 謂如有一，親近善士，於聖法中已成聰慧，於聖法中已得調順。於苦聖諦如實知苦，於集聖諦如實知集，於滅聖諦如實知滅，於道聖諦如實知道。既得成就有學智見，從此已後漸修聖道，遍於三界見修所斷一切法中，自能離繫、自得解脫。如是便能超過三界。如是名為由出世道而趣離欲。
items.en: It is like one who, drawing near a good teacher, becomes wise within the noble Dharma, and becomes well-tamed within the noble Dharma — knowing suffering, as it truly is, as the noble truth of suffering; knowing its origin, as it truly is, as the noble truth of origin; knowing its cessation, as it truly is, as the noble truth of cessation; and knowing the path, as it truly is, as the noble truth of the path. …Having thus attained a trainee's knowledge and vision, one thereafter gradually cultivates the noble path, and, throughout the three realms, with regard to everything to be abandoned by seeing and by cultivation, one is oneself able to become free of its bonds, oneself attaining liberation. In this way, one is able to transcend the three realms entirely. This is called setting out towards detachment by the supramundane path.

items.title: Section: The Fourteen Provisions Open — Moral Discipline, and Its Own Rich Sixfold Structure

items.zh: 云何名為二道資糧？嗢拕南曰：自他圓滿、善法欲、戒、根律儀、食知量、覺寤、正知住、善友、聞、思、無障、捨、莊嚴。謂若自圓滿、若他圓滿、若善法欲、若戒律儀、若根律儀、若於食知量、若初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽、若正知而住、若善友性、若聞正法、若思正法、若無障礙、若修惠捨、若沙門莊嚴。如是等法、是名世間及出世間諸離欲道趣向資糧。當知此中，若自圓滿、若他圓滿、若善法欲，此三如前修集種子諸劣緣中，已辨其相。云何戒律儀？嗢拕南曰：戒律儀，當知辨三、虧滿十、六異門、三淨、勝功德十種。戒律儀者，謂如有一，安住具戒，廣說乃至受學學處。云何名為安住具戒？謂於所受學所有學處。不虧身業，不虧語業，無缺，無穿。如是名為安住具戒。
items.en: What are the provisions for both paths? The summary verse says: self-perfection, perfection by others, a wish for the good; moral discipline, restraint of the faculties, moderation in eating; wakefulness, clear awareness, abiding with good companions; hearing and reflecting on the Dharma, freedom from obstruction, relinquishment, and adornment. …It should be understood that, among these, self-perfection, perfection by others, and a wish for the good have already had their marks explained above, among the lesser conditions for cultivating the seed [of lineage]. …What is moral discipline in its proper restraint? The summary verse says: moral discipline should be understood through distinguishing three, ten marks of impairment and ten of fulfilment, six alternate names, three purities, and ten excellent virtues. …Moral discipline in its proper restraint is that one abides in complete discipline — and so on at length, down to training in every point of training. What is called abiding in complete discipline? It is that, regarding all the points of training one has undertaken, one's bodily conduct is not impaired, one's verbal conduct is not impaired, nothing is lacking, and nothing is breached. This is called abiding in complete discipline.

items.title: Guarding Each Precept Individually, and the Fivefold Map of Monastic Law

items.zh: 云何名為善能守護別解脫律儀？謂能守護七眾所受別解脫律儀。即此律儀，眾差別故，成多律儀。今此義中，唯依苾芻律儀處說善能守護別解脫律儀。云何名為軌則圓滿？謂如有一，或於威儀路，或於所作事，或於善品加行處所，成就軌則。隨順世間，不越世間；隨順毘奈耶，不越毘奈耶。云何名為於威儀路成就軌則，隨順世間，不越世間；隨順毘奈耶，不越毘奈耶？
items.en: What is called skilfully guarding the prātimokṣa restraint? It is being able to guard the prātimokṣa restraint belonging to the sevenfold assembly. Because this very restraint differs according to each assembly, it becomes many restraints. In the present sense, it is only with regard to the monk's and nun's restraint that this skilful guarding is spoken of. What is called perfected protocol? It is that, whether in the pathways of deportment, or in the tasks one performs, or in the settings for applying oneself to wholesome practice, one accomplishes proper protocol — conforming to worldly convention, not exceeding worldly convention; conforming to the Vinaya, not exceeding the Vinaya.

items.title: Perfected Protocol in Practice: Posture, and the Texture of Ordinary Monastic Life

items.zh: 謂如有一，於所應行、於如所行，即於此中如是而行。由是行故，不為世間之所譏毀，不為賢良、正至、善士、諸同法者、諸持律者、諸學律者之所呵責。如於所行，於其所住、所坐、所臥，當知亦爾。如是名為於威儀路成就軌則，隨順世間，不越世間；隨順毘奈耶，不越毘奈耶。云何名為於所作事成就軌則，隨順世間，不越世間；隨順毘奈耶，不越毘奈耶？謂如有一，於其所作，若衣服事、若便利事、若用水事、若楊枝事、若入聚落行乞食事、若受用事、若盪鉢事、若安置事、若洗足事、若為敷設臥具等事。即此略說衣事、鉢事，復有所餘如是等類諸所應作，名所作事。
items.en: It is that one, regarding what should be done and how it should be done, acts accordingly in every case. Because of acting in this way, one is not disparaged by the world, and is not reproached by good persons — the virtuous and those who have arrived at the truth — by fellow practitioners, by those who uphold the Vinaya, or by those who study the Vinaya. Just as with walking, so too it should be understood regarding standing, sitting, and lying down. …It is that one, in what one does, attends to matters of clothing, of relieving oneself, of using water, of tooth-cleaning, of entering a village to beg for alms, of making use of things, of rinsing the bowl, of storing it, of washing the feet, and of arranging one's bedding and the like. This is a brief account of matters of robes and of the bowl; there are, further, other such matters that should likewise be attended to — these are called "the tasks one performs."

items.zh: 如其所應，於所應作、於如所作，即於此中如是而作。由是作故，不為世間之所譏毀，不為賢良、正至、善士、諸同法者、諸持律者、諸學律者之所呵責。如是名為於所作事成就軌則，隨順世間，不越世間；隨順毘奈耶，不越毘奈耶。云何名為於諸善品加行處所成就軌則，隨順世間，不越世間；隨順毘奈耶，不越毘奈耶？
items.en: As is appropriate, in whatever is to be done and in the manner in which it is to be done, one acts accordingly in just this way. Because of acting in this way, one is not disparaged by the world, and is not reproached by the virtuous, by those who have rightly arrived, by good persons, by fellow practitioners of the same Dharma, by those who uphold the Vinaya, or by those who study the Vinaya. This is called accomplishing proper protocol in the tasks one performs — conforming to worldly convention, not exceeding worldly convention; conforming to the Vinaya, not exceeding the Vinaya. What is called accomplishing proper protocol in the settings for applying oneself to wholesome practice — conforming to worldly convention, not exceeding worldly convention; conforming to the Vinaya, not exceeding the Vinaya?

blocks.text: The third part of the Śrāvaka Stage, the **Stage of Departure** (出離地), describes how one actually sets out towards liberation. It starts with two paths, then lists fourteen "provisions" for the journey and explains the first, moral discipline, at length. Ru-Yi translates this fascicle almost completely.

One may become free of desire by the **mundane path** or by the **supramundane path**. Venerable Miào Jìng: after access concentration, one has two roads. Master Cháng Bǎi: the mundane path keeps afflictions from appearing but does not uproot them: "like a stone pressing on grass".

The mundane path: one sees each lower level as coarse and each higher as peaceful, and rises level by level, through the absorptions up to the peak of existence. Master Cháng Bǎi: the lower level has more faults; that is "coarseness".

The supramundane path: knowing suffering as suffering, through the path as path, one attains the trainee's knowledge and cuts afflictions by seeing and cultivation. Their seeds are not merely stored away but "burnt", never to sprout again. Venerable Miào Jìng: the path of seeing cuts conceptual self-clinging; the path of cultivation, innate self-clinging.

The provisions for both paths are fourteen: one's own perfection, perfection by others, the wish for the good, moral discipline, sense restraint, moderation in eating, wakefulness, clear awareness, good friendship, hearing and reflecting on the Dharma, freedom from obstacles, generosity, adornment of the renunciant, and so on. Venerable Miào Jìng counts generosity and "adornment" as two items.

Moral discipline has six aspects: abiding in it, guarding the prātimokṣa, perfect protocol, perfect conduct, seeing danger in the slightest fault, and undertaking the training. Venerable Miào Jìng: losing mindfulness and breaking a minor precept, but at once repenting and being restored, counts as "nothing breached".

Perfect protocol covers posture, tasks such as dressing, washing, cleaning one's teeth, going for alms. Master Cháng Bǎi's practical advice: in shared quarters, do not open and close doors loudly; when speaking, notice whether others are asleep.

quiz.q: Where do the mundane and supramundane paths diverge, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: after attaining access concentration there are two roads; one is mundane detachment, cultivating form-realm absorption
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: after attaining access concentration one has two roads: one is detachment by the mundane path — cultivating form-realm absorption. The other is the supramundane path of contemplating the four truths.

quiz.q: The note calls "a stone pressing down grass" the treatise's own image. What does Master Cháng Bǎi's lecture show?
options: it is the lecturer's own image — mundane detachment suppresses affliction by concentration without uprooting it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: afflictions like desire, hatred, and harming are overcome by concentration, kept from manifesting, but not uprooted — like a stone pressing on grass. The treatise here has no such image; the note mistook the lecturer's words for the text.

quiz.q: Into what method does Master Cháng Bǎi expand the coarse-and-peaceful contemplation?
options: the six-aspect contemplation — the lower as coarse, painful, obstructive; the higher as peaceful, excellent, free
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the lower as coarse, painful, obstructive — after observing it, revulsion arises; the higher as peaceful, excellent, free — after observing it, delight arises. Venerable Miào Jìng speaks only of the two marks, coarse and peaceful.

quiz.q: How do the two paths differ in effect on affliction? The note calls the burnt-seed image the treatise's own — is it?
options: the mundane path only suppresses, the supramundane destroys the seeds; the burnt-seed image is cited by Cháng Bǎi from fascicle 51, not in this fascicle's text
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mundane path can only suppress afflictions, which still arise; only the supramundane path permanently destroys their seeds. He cites the image of seeds burnt by fire from fascicle 51; the note presents it as this fascicle's own.

quiz.q: The summary verse's last term "捨莊嚴" is rendered "the adornments of renunciation." What problem does this cause?
options: it is two items — generosity and the recluse's adornments; merged, the fourteen become thirteen
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: in all there are fourteen; the provisions have fourteen sections. "捨莊嚴" should be two items, generosity and adornment; merged in the English, the count falls short.

quiz.q: How do the masters explain "nothing breached" (無穿) in abiding in complete discipline?
options: Miào Jìng: an occasional lapse is at once repented and purity restored; Cháng Bǎi: keeping precepts like an unpunctured balloon
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if, losing mindfulness, you break a few precepts and at once repent and are restored to purity, that is "nothing breached." Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping one's precepts like a balloon never punctured — that is "nothing breached."

quiz.q: The English lists "good persons" as a separate class. How do the masters distinguish 賢良、正至、善士?
options: Miào Jìng: diligent practitioners before stream-entry are the virtuous, the four fruits are the arrived, and "good persons" covers them all; Cháng Bǎi: the arrived are noble ones who reached nirvāṇa
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "the arrived" are noble ones — the four fruits; those diligently practising before stream-entry are "the virtuous"; all these are "good persons." Master Cháng Bǎi: noble ones from stream-entry to arhatship are "the arrived."
